reason: An actress who exists only inside the worlds she was made for finds herself in a Western beside an orc from another genre entirely. Avaren's comedy turns a basic condition of generated film, characters written into whatever scene is asked of them, into the story itself; it was made for the Higgsfield Talent Contest and produced by The Blue Horizon.

Dair Karakeev returns to the survivor and dog of his 51-minute GOOD BOY with a 32-minute first episode: Argos's newborn pups need vaccines, and the search leads Jane to an abandoned research station. Magnific commissioned the sequel, and the release credits a small team for producing, sound and cinematography.

An alien ship over a quiet Japanese city turns out to be on an errand: two visitors have come to collect a vintage car from an old takoyaki seller. Allan Ripley shapes the comedy in the look of 1990s TV anime and names each tool by role, from Seedance 2.5 video to Dehancer colour.

A sinking river gives back one soldier of a thousand-year-old clay army, and a village has to decide what it is guarding against. The 22-minute first episode is built in titled chapters, and the studio's director's note frames the army as a promise rather than a weapon.
Babel’s one-life-for-one-home rule now runs through three complete films. The new HUSH returns Mercy as an auditor of a factory that sells quiet, widening the city’s system from housing to sleep.
